<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par60" />{{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}}, however, it is shortened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמָרְךָ}} (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמְרֶ֫ךָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמְרֶ֫ךָּ}}; with ''Nûn energicum'', see {{GHGpar|58|i}}), {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמָרְכֶם}}, &c. Instead of {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלוּ}}<ref>This form is also found as feminine without a suffix, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=7}}. In the latter passage {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּקְרְבוּ}} is probably to be regarded, with König, as a clumsy correction of the original {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּק׳}}, intended to suggest the reading {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּקְרַ֫בְנָה}}, to agree with the usual gender of {{GHGheb|text=עֲצָמוֹת}}.</ref> is used for the 2nd and 3rd ''fem. plur''. before suffixes in three places: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|b}}
Rem. 1. {{GHGheb|text=יְחָבְרְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=20}} is an anomalous form for {{GHGheb|text=יַחְבָּרְךָ}} (cf. the analogous {{GHGheb|text=יָחְנְךָ}} {{GHGpar|67|n}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יִֽפְגָֽשְׁךָ}} (so Baer; others {{GHGheb|text=יִפְגָּֽשְׁךָ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִפְגָּֽשֲׁךָ}}. To the same category as {{GHGheb|text=יְחָבְרְךָ}} belong also, according to the usual explanation, {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽעָבְדֵם}} (from {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲבֹד}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=9}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָֽעָב׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=3}}. As a matter of fact, the explanation of these forms as imperfects of {{GHGterm|Qal}} appears to be required by the last of these passages; yet why has the retraction of the ''ŏ'' taken place only in these examples (beside numerous forms like {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַבְדֵ֫נִי}})? Could the Masora in the two Decalogues and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=24}} (on the analogy of which {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=3}} was then wrongly pointed) have intended an imperfect {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} with the suffix, meaning {{GHGtranslate|thou shalt not allow thyself to be brought to worship them}}?

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|c}}
Verbs which have ''a'' in the second syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, and imperative, {{GHGterm|Qal}} (to which class especially {{GHGterm|verba tertiae}} and {{GHGterm|mediae gutturalis}} belong, {{GHGpar|64}} and {{GHGpar|65}}) do ''not'', as a rule, change the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (nor of the imperative, see {{GHGpar|61|g}}) into {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before suffixes; but the Pathaḥ, coming to stand in an open syllable before the tone, is lengthened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִגְאָל֫וּהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=5|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁלָחֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֻ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=18}}; but {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}}, is probably a {{GHGterm|forma mixta|en=mixed form}} combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|74|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|d}}
2. Not infrequently suffixes with the connecting vowel ''a'' are also found with the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּדְבָּקַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=19}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=24}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=18}}; also {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫נִּי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=19.31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (in principal {{GHGterm|pause}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכִּירָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=33}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=20|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַכִּירָ֑נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=16}} (manifestly owing to the influence of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=יְדָעָ֫נוּ}}); {{GHGheb|text=יִלְבָּשָׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=8}}; even {{GHGheb|text=אֲמִילַֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=10–12|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּֽוֹשִׁיעָן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יְחִיתַֽן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=17}} (where, however, the ancient versions read {{GHGheb|text=יְחִתֶּ֫ךָ}}); even {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדְּפוֹ}} (''ô'' from ''āhu'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=4}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּצְפְּנֵם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (where, however, the text is corrupt); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=6}} (where read with the old versions {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}} (see {{GHGpar|74|e}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=12}}.—On pausal {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} for {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲבָֽרֲכָֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=9}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַֽלֲצֶ֑הוּ}} (so Baer, but ed. Mant., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַלְצֵ֑הוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}, see {{GHGpar|29|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|e}}
3. Suffixes are also appended in twelve passages to the plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַכְּאוּנַ֫נִי}}, {{GHGtranslate|will ye break me in pieces}}? {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְשָֽׁרְת֑וּנֶךְ}} (here necessarily with a connecting vowel) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=7.10}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=22}} ({{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} but probably corrupt); elsewhere always without a connecting vowel; {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֻ֫נְנִי}} with two other examples {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=15}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=־֫וּנְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=־ֻ֫נְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=־֫וּנְהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=24}}, all in principal pause. [See Böttcher, ''Lehrb.'', § 1047 f.]

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|f}}
4. In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}}, and {{GHGterm|Poʿlēl}}, the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} of the final syllable, like the ''ō'' in Qal, becomes vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; but before the suffixes {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}} it is shortened to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְקַבֶּצְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=2}}. With a final guttural, however, {{GHGheb|text=אֲשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=27}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=8}}, where with Qimḥi {{GHGheb|text=תְּכַבֵּ֫דְךָ}} is to be read. ''ē'' is<section end="par60" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
